This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump is in Texas again trying to rally support for Republican Ken Paxton's Senate campaign against Democrat James Tallarico.
He's never going to love me, and he's never going to love oil and gas,
and he's never going to love your Second Amendment,
and he's never going to love your children the way you do.
It's a different kind of love.
You can't put this guy, you can't have a vote like that.
It's too close.
That's Trump and Corpus Christi last hour, who'll also appear in Lubbock later.
This marks his fourth visit to Texas since September,
highlighting the state's importance to Republicans.
Texas has been a Republican stronghold for decades,
but Tallarico's outreach and Paxton's political and personal struggles have made it a battleground.
More than 30 million Americans have already voted with Election Day one week from today.
As NPR's Tamara Keith reports, if you feel like you've seen too many campaign ads,
there's a reason.
According to Ad Impact, this has officially become the most expensive election cycle ever when it comes to campaign ads.
The tally is up to $11.22 billion with a B for ads already run and reservations through Election Day.
Republicans have about a $400 million advantage.
The Texas Senate is the most expensive race in the country, with the Ohio Senate race a close second.
Both have seen ad spending of more than half a billion dollars.
The staggering sum surpassed the 2024 campaign, which included congressional races and a presidential race.
They cost more than $3 billion on its own.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
Voting has closed in Israel's election.
Turnout was high in what's widely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership.
He's facing a challenge from former military chief Gadi Eisenkot.
Exit polls show no clear winner, likely setting off weeks of jockeying before a leader is declared.
The election is Israel's first national vote since the October 7th attack.
The price that store owners pay for processing debit card transactions could soon be going down.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports on the latest twist in a long-running battle that pits retailers against debit card issuers.
Every time a customer uses a debit card to make a purchase, the seller has to pay a fee to the bank that issued the debit card,
typically 21 cents plus a fraction of the value of the sale.
Last year, those swipe fees added up to more than $40 billion.
Now a federal appeals court has ruled the fees must come down.
The court found the Federal Reserve, which regulates the fees,
had allowed the issuing banks to recoup costs Congress never intended.
A coalition of retailers welcomed the decision, which could result in lower costs for consumers.
Meanwhile, an even bigger fight continues over the swipe fees charged on credit cards,
which are currently unregulated and cost merchants almost four times as much as debit fees.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
A.I. stocks led Wall Street higher today.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Utah authorities say DNA connects serial killer Ted Bundy to the death of a teenager more than 50 years after her body was discovered by a hunter.
Bundy has been dead since 1989, but the tally of his confirmed victims continues to grow due to advances in DNA testing.
He killed at least 30 women and girls in multiple states in the 1970s.
Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in women.
Now a coalition of leading medical groups has released a new framework for doctors to identify risks to women's heart health, starting in childhood.
NPR's Maria Godoy has more.
Throughout their lives, women experience hormonal changes that influence heart health in ways men don't experience.
The new framework identifies key life stages that offer windows of opportunity to prevent heart disease and stroke.
For example, pregnancy complications like gestational diabetes can unmask heart risks while changes in cholesterol and metabolic health during perimenopause can also be early signs of cardiovascular risk.
The guidance comes from the American Medical Association, the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the Society for Maternal Fetal Medicine.
It appears in the journal Circulation.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
Jay-Z has picked himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show on February 14th at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.
His Rock Nation Entertainment Company has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to produce the halftime show.
Jay-Z has won 25 Grammy Awards and received 89 nominations, the second most in history behind his wife, Beyonce.
